primary_meaning: evil, sin, spiritual blindness/ignorance, death, and separation from or opposition to God (as the antithesis of divine light)
primary_basis: John 1:5 (light shines in the darkness; darkness has not overcome it)
John 3:19-21 (people loved darkness rather than light because deeds were evil)
1 John 1:5-6 (God is light; in him is no darkness; walking in darkness is lying)
Ephesians 5:8-11 (once darkness, now light in the Lord; unfruitful works of darkness)
Colossians 1:13 (delivered from the domain of darkness)
Acts 26:18 (turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God)
Isaiah 9:2 / Matthew 4:16 (people dwelling in darkness have seen a great light)

alternatives.meaning: eschatological judgment, wrath, or cosmic upheaval accompanying the Day of the Lord
primordial chaos, formlessness, or the uncreated state before God's ordering word
divine hiddenness, mystery, or the unapproachable presence of God (sometimes called 'divine darkness')
literal physical night, absence of sunlight, or ordinary obscurity without moral weight

notes: Light/darkness dualism is one of the most consistent symbolic polarities across Old and New Testament literature and subsequent Christian teaching; the moral-spiritual reading of darkness as evil/sin/separation from God is the dominant and settled primary sense in preaching, catechesis, and standard commentaries, even while secondary nuances (judgment, chaos, mystery) are also widely recognized.
